{"id":"bd2656cd-d730-440b-8d95-462c892b2149","object":"chat.completion","created":1790500437,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"requirements":[{"requirement_id":"R1","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C2"]},{"requirement_id":"R2","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C1","C2"]},{"requirement_id":"R3","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R4","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]},{"requirement_id":"R5","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C2"]},{"requirement_id":"R6","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]}]}","reasoning_content":"We need answer reconcile fixed Task Skeleton with Verified Claims. Need output JSON. Need evaluate each requirement.

We have Original Question and Task Skeleton requirements R1-R6. Verified Claims C1, C2.

Need assign statuses exactly one per requirement, supported_by claims.

Let's parse.

Original Question: Every year teams ... compete in final of prestigious programming contest for prestigious title. In one particular year, I discovered that a team featuring an Australian coder won championship. This coder has impressive track record ... bronze, silver, gold, another silver in four consecutive IOIs. His other two teammates were from same country. Could you tell me the year associated with competition title and name of host university for the year he won that title?

Task Skeleton:
R1: Every year, teams of competitive programmers from universities around the world compete in the final of a prestigious programming contest for the prestigious title.
R2: In one particular year, I discovered that a team featuring an Australian coder won the championship.
R3: This coder has ... secured bronze, silver, gold, and another silver medal in four consecutive IOIs.
R4: His other two teammates were from the same country.
R5: Could you tell me the year associated with the competition title
R6: and the name of the host university for the year he won that title?

Verified Claims:
C1: Jerry Mao is Australian competitive programmer who won bronze at IOI 2015, silver IOI 2016, gold IOI 2017, silver IOI 2018.
C2: Jerry Mao was member of MIT team MIT ZEROONE (with Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao), which won ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 Nov 2022) as World Champion.

Need status each.

R1: General statement about contest. Claims don't mention general annual competition? C2 mentions ICPC World Finals, team from MIT won as World Champion. Does it establish "Every year, teams ... compete in final of prestigious programming contest for prestigious title"? C2 only specific ICPC 2021 World Finals. It might partially support that there is a prestigious programming contest? But R1 is broad "Every year..." The claims don't establish annual universality, teams worldwide, final, prestigious title. Maybe C2 supports "team from university competed in ICPC World Finals" but not general every year. Need assess material semantic conditions. R1: every year, teams of competitive programmers from universities around world compete in final of prestigious programming contest for prestigious title. C2 supports specific instance: MIT team won ICPC World Finals 2021 as World Champion. That implies a team of competitive programmers from university competed in final of ICPC (a programming contest) and won title. But not "every year", "around the world", "prestigious" maybe. Partially supported? It establishes at least one substantive material part: teams from universities compete in final of programming contest for title. But not annual/all world/prestigious. Since C2 says MIT team won World Champion, it establishes a team from university won a programming contest final. So R1 partially supported.

But need be careful: R1 maybe background context not central? We must status. Could be unsupported if no claim about every year. But partially_supported definition: establishes at least one substantive material part. It does establish a team of competitive programmers from a university competed/won final of programming contest. So partial likely.

R2: In one particular year, team featuring Australian coder won championship. C1 says Jerry Mao is Australian competitive programmer. C2 says Jerry Mao was member of MIT team that won ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka as World Champion. So yes fully supported: team featuring Australian coder (Jerry Mao) won championship (ICPC World Finals 2021). Note "in one particular year" C2 says ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka held 10 Nov 2022. The team won championship. So R2 fully supported by C1,C2. supported_by ["C1","C2"].

R3: coder has bronze, silver, gold, another silver in four consecutive IOIs. C1 exactly: Jerry Mao won bronze IOI 2015, silver IOI 2016, gold IOI 2017, silver IOI 2018. Fully supported by C1.

R4: His other two teammates were from same country. C2: teammate names Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao. But does it establish they were from same country? No. It says Jerry Mao Australian, teammates Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao. Names might suggest? But no outside knowledge. C2 doesn't state their nationality/country. R4 requires other two teammates from same country (same as Jerry? Australia). Claims do not establish. Maybe C2 says MIT team with Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao, but no countries. So unsupported. supported_by [].

R5: Could you tell me the year associated with the competition title? This is question/request. The requirement likely asks to identify year associated with competition title he won. Need see claims: C2 says ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022). The "year associated with competition title" could be 2021 or 2022? They ask "year associated with competition title" and "host university for the year he won that title". In ICPC, 2021 World Finals held in Dhaka in 2022. Need determine if Claim supports. C2 states won ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022). So year associated with competition title could be 2021. It explicitly says ICPC 2021 World Finals. So R5 fully supported? It asks "Could you tell me the year associated with the competition title". C2 provides "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka" and won. So yes, year is 2021 (or event held 2022). But original question: "the year associated with the competition title" likely the contest year (2021). Claim C2 states "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022)". That gives year 2021 associated with title. Fully supported by C2. But maybe R5 is just interrogative, not a fact. In previous tasks, requirements from question asking for answer should be supported if claim gives answer. Yes.

R6: name of host university for the year he won that title. Need host university. C2: team MIT won ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka. Does it state host university? No, it says host city Dhaka? "World Finals Dhaka" likely host is Dhaka? University? It does not mention host university. It mentions MIT is the team's university, not host. So unsupported. Wait "host university" could refer to the university hosting the competition final. C2 doesn't say. So unsupported. supported_by [].

Need consider R1 maybe fully supported? No. R1 general statement maybe C2 partially. Need decide if partial or unsupported. The rules: Mere topical relevance does not count. C2 establishes a specific instance of a team from a university (MIT) winning ICPC World Finals (a programming contest). That is a substantive material part of R1? R1: "Every year, teams of competitive programmers from universities around the world compete in the final of a prestigious programming contest for the prestigious title." Material parts: (a) annual competition, (b) teams from universities around world, (c) compete in final, (d) prestigious programming contest, (e) for prestigious title. C2: specific ICPC World Finals, team MIT, won as World Champion. It supports (c) compete in final? It says won World Finals. Thus competed in final. It supports teams from universities (MIT). It supports prestigious programming contest? "ICPC World Finals" and "World Champion" implies prestige? But not explicit "prestigious". It does not support "every year" or "around the world" or "teams of competitive programmers" maybe. So partial. Could also be unsupported if R1 is just background and not central. But definition partial if at least one substantive material part. Yes.

Need ensure no other claims. Let's format JSON only.

Need include all requirements exactly once. Use statuses.

Let's produce:

  "requirements": [
    {"requirement_id": "R1", "status": "partially_supported", "supported_by": ["C2"]},

    {"requirement_id": "R6", "status": "unsupported", "supported_by": []}
  ]
}

Double-check R5: "Could you tell me the year associated with the competition title" It might also need "year he won that title" from C2. C2 says ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held 2022). If "year associated with competition title" could be 2021. Yes. If asked "year associated with competition title and name of host university for the year he won that title" - the year is in C2. Fully.

R6: host university. C2 doesn't mention. Unsupported.

Potential issue: R4 "His other two teammates were from the same country." C2 names teammates Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao. Could "Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao" both Chinese names? But no outside knowledge. Also "same country" maybe Australia? C1 says Jerry Mao Australian. C2 doesn't state teammates' country. So unsupported.

Potential issue: R1 "Every year..." C2 says "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022) as World Champion." Does it support "teams of competitive programmers from universities around the world compete in the final"? It only mentions MIT team, no around the world. But at least one team. Partial.
